content:
We need to return all possible precursors of applying the template (template_id 1914384) to the given molecule (initial_molecule). The template is given with mapped_rxn: "([CH3:1]/[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)=[CH:9]/[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C:13](=[O:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18])>>([CH3:1][C@H:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18])"

So forward reaction: substrate (left) -> product (right). The product is the given initial_molecule? Let's check: product SMILES: [CH3:1][C@H:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

Yes matches initial_molecule (with stereochemistry). So we need to apply the template in reverse (retrosynthetic) to get precursors (reactants). The template's left side is the precursor(s) combined? It appears a single precursor (maybe a single molecule) that undergoes transformation to product. The left side: ([CH3:1]/[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)=[CH:9]/[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C:13](=[O:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18])

That is a single molecule with a double bond between C2 and CH9? Actually it's a conjugated system: CH3 attached to C2 which is attached to aromatic ring and double bond to CH9 which is attached to chain etc. So the precursor is a single molecule.

Thus applying template in reverse yields that precursor SMILES. We need to return list of lists of precursors. Likely only one combination: the precursor SMILES.

We can use apply_template tool to get outcomes. Let's call apply_template with molecule_smiles = initial_molecule, template_id = "1914384".
